recognize_zh: 骨髓與肝臟切片的巨噬細胞胞質內擠滿許多細小圓點狀的無鞭毛體（amastigote，放大圖可見核與動基體），免疫染色顯示巨噬細胞內棕色顆粒狀陽性，即使血清學陰性仍支持內臟利什曼原蟲病。
features: Bone marrow macrophage containing numerous small round to oval intracytoplasmic organisms (arrow, inset)
Organisms about 2-4 micrometers with a dot-like nucleus and adjacent kinetoplast visible at high magnification
Liver section: Kupffer cell/macrophage distended by abundant intracellular amastigotes (arrow, inset)
Immunostain shows granular brown positivity of organisms within macrophages in marrow and liver
Background marrow with erythroid and myeloid precursors; no well-formed granulomas in the fields shown
describe_en: Bone marrow biopsy shows a cellular marrow in which macrophages contain numerous small round to oval intracytoplasmic organisms with a punctate nucleus and kinetoplast. A liver biopsy shows Kupffer cells/macrophages distended by similar abundant intracellular organisms. Immunohistochemistry demonstrates granular positivity of the intracellular organisms in both the marrow and liver sections. Findings are consistent with visceral leishmaniasis with bone marrow and hepatic involvement, despite negative serology; PCR confirmation and speciation are recommended.

ddx.vs: Histoplasma yeasts are similar in size but have a clear halo, lack a kinetoplast, and stain with GMS and PAS.
Toxoplasma tachyzoites are crescent-shaped and lack a kinetoplast, forming pseudocysts in various cell types rather than filling macrophages.
T. cruzi amastigotes also have a kinetoplast but are found mainly in cardiac and smooth muscle cells rather than marrow and hepatic macrophages.
Talaromyces yeasts divide by fission with a central transverse septum and are GMS-positive, lacking a kinetoplast.
